issues.legal_issue: A claimant seeking a permanent injunction to prevent interference with property must prove actual physical possession on the date the suit is filed, and cannot establish that possession merely through inferences from surrounding circumstances.
material_facts: The claimant sued for a permanent injunction, asserting that he was a tenant in possession and was carrying on businesses at the premises.

The trial court found that the claimant had not proved actual possession or the businesses he claimed to operate; the premises were found unfit for business, and there was no adequate evidence that he had repaired them.
The claimant had not paid rent for many years and did not rebut the evidence supporting the contention that he had vacated the premises.

The lower appellate court inferred possession from the withdrawal of an earlier suit and the absence of evidence showing that possession had been handed over; the Supreme Court held that this did not establish possession on the date of the later suit.
issues.conclusion: The claimant had not proved actual and lawful possession on the date of suit and was not entitled to a permanent injunction. The appeal was allowed, the High Court judgment was set aside, and the suit was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 38 of the Specific Relief Act, permanent injunction restraining interference with possession may be granted only where the claimant proves actual and physical possession on the date of suit. The burden is on the claimant; possession cannot be established merely by drawing inferences from circumstances. A claimant seeking this equitable relief must also show lawful possession. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.injunction_suit: The claimant brought a suit seeking a permanent injunction to prevent another person from interfering with claimed possession of property.
predicates.actual_possession_not_proved: The claimant did not establish actual and physical possession of the property on the date the suit was filed.
predicates.lawful_possession_not_established: The claimant did not establish that the claimed possession was lawful.

issues.definition: In a suit seeking a permanent injunction against interference with property, if actual possession or lawful possession is not established, the injunction is denied.
